note: Re-quoted 2026-11-25 to the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0; library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz, read offline as owb-am), per the founder decision of 2026-11-18 (Amharic quotes OWB everywhere). This supersedes what the notes below say about the 1962 UBS Bible and about wording borrowed from other Amharic works: every `mined` row is now a verbatim OWB span in its block (exact OWB pieces may be joined with '…'); `self_rendered` rows are allusions and paraphrases left as the translator's prose, each with its `why`. This pass finished the 2026-11-18 re-quote: the nine prose recitations still in 1962 wording (Eph 3:20, John 5:44, 1 John 1:3, Rom 8:31, Col 1:26, Heb 13:8 twice, Luke 14:11, Heb 4:9) now carry OWB's words, 2 Kings 6:16 is split into OWB's two quoted pieces, the Luke 6:23 quotation closes before Smith's own Rom 8:17 paraphrase, and 38 OWB quotations the notes missed are recorded.

Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), quoted verbatim from the bundled owb-am text (backend/library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz), per the founder decision of 2026-11-18 that every Amharic work quotes OWB. Re-quoted 2026-11-18: every quotation of Scripture, marked or recited without quote marks, was replaced with the OWB words (whole verse, joined range, or the shortest contiguous OWB span carrying the quoted clause), spliced by script; citations and quote marks are as the translator wrote them.

A `mined` row citing OWB is verbatim OWB in that block. A `self_rendered` row is either a quotation whose OWB words were re-personed to fit how Hannah Whitall Smith applies the verse (or, at Matt 6:27, a paraphrase whose argument needs KJV 'stature'), or an allusion or paraphrase in her own voice, which stays prose. Allusion rows written before the re-quote keep their earlier status; the 9 still citing the 1962 Amharic Bible are such prose allusions, not quotations, and carry no quoted verse text.
